one_liner: Header-only C++17 mesh-processing library (booleans, intersection curves, spatial trees, remeshing) that the vendor measures 2-233x faster than CGAL, libigl, MeshLib and nanoflann.
what_it_does: trueform is a geometry library for triangle and polygon meshes and point clouds. It covers booleans and N-ary CSG arrangements, mesh-mesh intersection curves, self-intersections, AABB/OBB/OBBRSS trees for collision, distance and k-NN, topology (connected components, boundary paths, half-edges), ICP, curvature, isocontours, decimation and remeshing, and a volume/SDF module. The API is free functions over zero-copy views of your own buffers: tf::make_points/make_faces/make_polygons wrap flat arrays, and structures are attached with tags (polygons | tf::tag(tree) | tf::tag(frame)) before calls such as tf::make_boolean, tf::make_intersection_curves or tf::neighbor_search. It is not a drop-in for CGAL: there is no Surface_mesh, kernel or property-map interface. Python (NumPy) and TypeScript/WASM bindings expose the same engine.
how_it_is_fast: Coordinates are scaled onto an int32/int64 lattice, and every orientation and intersection predicate is evaluated in exact integer arithmetic. This avoids CGAL's lazy/rational number types while still classifying contacts into five canonical types (VV, VE, VF, EE, EF) and arranging each cut face in its own plane; disagreeing observations are resolved by 'topological aggregation', a majority vote within a manifold-edge-connected unit (Sajovic and Knez, arXiv 2607.15905). Most algorithms run in parallel on oneTBB (parallel union-find for components, partitioned edge collapse for decimation, k-ring quadric fitting for curvature) and allocate through a vendored mimalloc. Spatial trees are built once and reused under a rigid-transform tag, so a moving operand does not need a new tree.
when_to_use: Interactive or batch booleans and intersection curves on 10^5 to 10^6-triangle meshes on a multi-core machine: about 28 ms for a 2x1M union and 7 ms for 2x1M intersection curves on 16 M4 Max threads, with the tree already built
Repeated collision, distance or CSG queries against rigidly moving copies of the same mesh, where one prebuilt tree is reused through a tf::frame tag
Pipelines that hold geometry in flat arrays (C++ buffers, NumPy, browser TypedArrays) and want many operations from one library without converting to a half-edge type
Messy real-world meshes (non-manifold flaps, near-coincident walls): the 0.10.0 release notes report 1000/1000 closed, manifold results on the vendor's 1000-pair real-world corpus
Non-commercial, academic or evaluation work, or a team that will buy XLAB's commercial licence
when_not_to_use: Commercial, production or revenue-generating use without a paid agreement: the only public licence is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, which is not OSI-approved

Results that need exact rational output coordinates or provable exactness on the original floats (CGAL EPECK/Nef): trueform is exact on its integer lattice (float input maps to int32, double to int64), then rounds output back to float, and a non-zero tolerance moves vertices
Single-threaded or TBB-free environments: the headline numbers use 16 threads, and oneTBB is a hard dependency
One-off operations on meshes you will not query again: the repo's boolean and curve benchmarks build the AABB tree and topology outside the timer, so a cold call costs more than the headline figure
Code that needs a stable API: the library is 0.x and recent releases removed flags and reorganised modules (0.10.0 'module map (breaking)', 0.10.5 removed the resolve_* flags)

integration.dependencies: oneTBB (required); mimalloc 3.5.1 fetched and linked statically by default (TF_USE_MIMALLOC=OFF falls back to operator new); optional precompiled C++ facade (TF_BUILD_CPP), VTK integration; pip, Conan, NuGet and npm packages
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.16+; the benchmark suite builds as C++20; CI tests use Clang on Linux
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows (pip wheels built on all three, NuGet for Visual Studio), plus WebAssembly via npm @polydera/trueform; portable C++, -march=native only in the benchmarks
integration.thread_safety: not documented; algorithms parallelise internally with oneTBB (issue #5 still tracks wrapping the remaining direct tbb:: calls)

gotchas: Benchmarks are not like for like. In benchmarks/intersect and benchmarks/arrangement, trueform's AABB tree, face_membership and manifold_edge_link are built before timing, and the second operand is the same mesh under a rotation frame sharing that tree. CGAL's timed surface_intersection / corefine_and_compute_union call builds its own structures, and for the union it also copies both 1M-face Surface_meshes. trueform's own data puts one 1M-polygon AABB build at about 7.4 ms.

Correctness fixes are recent. v0.10.5 (Sep 2026) fixed N-operand 'within' builds that assigned every domain to operand 0 (shipped in 0.10.3-0.10.4), self-intersection split points placed on another operand's edges, and undefined behaviour from misaligned float loads in the binary STL reader. 0.10.0 fixed issue #21 (fit_similarity_alignment returned a scale n times too small). Pin a version and keep regression tests.

A system mimalloc must be built with MI_OVERRIDE=OFF and MI_ENABLE_LARGE_PAGES=0. Upstream's large-page default made a 16-thread process retain memory without bound (324 MB vs 156 MB over 200 graph builds), and ASAN builds force mimalloc off.
OBJ/STL path readers memory-map the file, so it must not change during the read
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against MeshLib (also source-available non-commercial, and trueform's boolean baseline), pick trueform for its wider set of composable primitives on raw arrays and reusable trees under rigid motion; pick Manifold when the licence must be permissive (Apache-2.0), and nanoflann for a permissive point k-NN index, even though trueform's OBB/OBBRSS trees beat it about 3x on single queries.
verified_claims_summary: Vendor-run benchmarks on an Apple M4 Max (16 threads, Clang -O3 -march=native) use the repo's benchmarks/ suite, which FetchContents CGAL 6.0.1 (with CGAL_LINKED_WITH_TBB), libigl 2.5.0, nanoflann 1.5.5, FCL 0.7.0, geogram 1.9.4 and Coal at its unpinned 'devel' branch, and reports the mean (curves, booleans, k-NN) or minimum (decimation, components) of 10 samples. The committed data at 1M polygons: union 27.8 ms vs CGAL corefinement 2,339 ms (about 84x, derived from page data) and MeshLib 161.5 ms (5.8x); k-NN on 512,872 points at k=10, 1.5 us (OBB/OBBRSS) vs nanoflann 4.5 us; mesh-mesh distance 0.20 ms (OBBRSS) vs Coal 0.47 ms. No MeshLib benchmark code is in the repo, so the 6x MeshLib figure cannot be reproduced from it, and the curves and boolean ratios exclude trueform's tree and topology build but include CGAL's.
status_note: Very active (v0.10.5 released 2026-09-21, last commit 2026-09-22, about 146 stars, nearly all commits by one author at XLAB/Polydera), but dual-licensed PolyForm Noncommercial or paid commercial. It is reference-only for this catalogue and cannot be copied into commercial code.
